findings.title: CLAUDE.md numbox pin (~=0.5.6) contradicts pyproject (>=0.5.13)
findings.description: CLAUDE.md 'Key dependencies' states `numbox~=0.5.6`, but pyproject.toml:13 pins `numbox>=0.5.13`. `~=0.5.6` means `>=0.5.6,<0.6` which is not even the same operator family, and the floor is 7 patch releases stale. The current @proxy tree depends on numbox APIs (proxy/proxy_if_available, the generic INT/INT eightbyte repack in call.py/abi.py) that only exist in newer numbox; 0.5.6 would not satisfy the code. The doc's stated minimum is simply wrong.
findings.impact: A contributor trusting CLAUDE.md could install/pin numbox 0.5.6 and hit import-time failures (missing proxy/repack machinery). The single source-of-truth pin lives in pyproject; the doc silently disagrees.
findings.recommendation: Change line 16 to `numbox>=0.5.13` (match pyproject.toml:13), or drop the explicit version from CLAUDE.md and point to pyproject as the source of truth.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md documents the removed @cres binding pattern; current tree uses @proxy
findings.description: The 'Adding a New Binding' code example (lines 33-37) and the Architecture step (line 26, 'wraps each function with `@cres` + `_call_lib_func`') and Related-Projects (line 86, numbox 'Provides ... `@cres` decorator') all describe a `@cres(signatures.get("duckdb_func"))` wrapper. The current ducklib.py imports and uses `from numbox.core.proxy.proxy import proxy, proxy_if_available` (ducklib.py:6) and every wrapper is `@proxy(signatures.get("name"), jit_options=jit_options)` (e.g. ducklib.py:276, 288, 1411). `@cres` appears nowhere in ducklib.py. The documented copy-paste template would not reproduce the real code: it omits `jit_options`, omits the `proxy_if_available` version-gating variant, and names a decorator the module no longer imports.
findings.impact: A new contributor following the documented 'Adding a New Binding' recipe writes a wrapper that does not match the codebase pattern (missing jit_options threading, wrong decorator), which is the single most-followed section for the project's core task.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite steps 2-3 and line 26/86 to the current pattern: `@proxy(signatures.get("duckdb_func"), jit_options=jit_options)` for always-present symbols and `@proxy_if_available(duckdb_lib, signatures.get(...), jit_options=jit_options)` for version-gated symbols, body `return _call_lib_func("duckdb_func", (arg,))`.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md 'Struct-by-value helpers' section lists ducklib.py helpers that no longer exist
findings.description: Lines 43-53 claim `ducklib.py` provides `_call_lib_func_struct_in`, `_call_lib_func_struct_out`, `_call_lib_func_byval`, `_emit_byval_call`, `_build_packed_interval`, and 'Custom `@intrinsic` functions ... for >16-byte structs'. In the current tree ducklib.py defines none of these: it imports only `_call_lib_func, _call_lib_func_byval` from numbox.core.bindings.call (ducklib.py:4), contains zero `@intrinsic` definitions, and struct-in/struct-out/byval/repack ABI handling all lives in numbox (call.py/abi.py), applied automatically by `_call_lib_func`. `_call_lib_func_struct_in`, `_call_lib_func_struct_out`, `_emit_byval_call`, and `_build_packed_interval` do not appear in ducklib.py at all. The interval repack the section attributes to a local `_build_packed_interval` is now numbox's generic `_repack_to_i64_pair`/`_needs_int_int_eightbyte_repack` in call.py.
findings.impact: Anyone searching ducklib.py for these named helpers to understand or extend struct-by-value handling finds nothing, and is misled about where ABI lowering happens (numbox, not ducklib).
findings.recommendation: Replace the section with a description of the actual current mechanism: struct-by-value/repack/sret handling is done by numbox's `_call_lib_func` (call.py/abi.py) based on the tuple-typed signatures in the `signatures` dict; ducklib.py only uses `_call_lib_func` and `_call_lib_func_byval`.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md 'Follow-ups' cites nonexistent ducklib.py line range 1525-1640 and an already-completed migration
findings.description: The Follow-ups item (lines 57-62) says to 'Migrate `_duckdb_bind_hugeint`/`_uhugeint`/`_interval` ... Three hand-rolled intrinsics at `ducklib.py:1525-1640` (~116 lines)' and references sibling wrappers at `ducklib.py:298-433`. ducklib.py is 1432 lines total, so lines 1525-1640 do not exist. Moreover the migration described as pending is already done: `duckdb_bind_hugeint` (ducklib.py:1411), `duckdb_bind_uhugeint` (1417), and `duckdb_bind_interval` (1423) are already plain `@proxy` + `_call_lib_func` wrappers with no bespoke intrinsics; the interval INT/INT repack the follow-up gates on ('once the numbox repack lands') already lives in numbox call.py. The entire follow-up is complete/obsolete.
findings.impact: The doc directs a maintainer to line ranges past EOF and to perform work that is already merged, wasting effort and eroding trust in the doc's line references.
findings.recommendation: Delete the Follow-ups item (the migration is done), or rewrite it to reflect that hugeint/uhugeint/interval binds are now @proxy wrappers at ducklib.py:1411-1432 and the numbox repack has landed.

findings.title: Adding-a-New-Binding steps 1/7 tell you to verify docstring links against duckdb.h, contradicting step 5 and the actual docstrings
findings.description: Step 1 (line 30) says 'Verify all docstring links point to the correct line in `duckdb.h`' and step 7 (line 41) says 're-verify ... docstring links against `duckdb.h`'. But step 5 (line 39) mandates 'Docstring links must use `https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/clients/c/api.html#func_name`, not links to `duckdb.h` source'. The actual code follows step 5: 191 docstrings in ducklib.py use the duckdb.org api.html anchor form (e.g. ducklib.py:1413), and none link to a duckdb.h line. So the instruction in steps 1 and 7 to verify docstring links against duckdb.h is self-contradictory with step 5 and does not match the codebase (docstring links have no line-in-duckdb.h to verify).
findings.impact: A contributor gets conflicting instructions on what a docstring link should point to, and step 1/7's 'verify against duckdb.h' cannot be satisfied for docstrings that (correctly, per step 5) point to duckdb.org.
findings.recommendation: Scope the duckdb.h verification in steps 1/7 to signatures/typedefs/parameter types only, and state that docstring links must point to duckdb.org (step 5); remove the 'docstring links point to the correct line in duckdb.h' phrasing from step 1.

notes: Verified against current tree: pyproject.toml pins numbox>=0.5.13 and duckdb>=1.3.2,<1.6; ducklib.py is 1432 lines and imports proxy/proxy_if_available + _call_lib_func/_call_lib_func_byval (no @cres, no local @intrinsic, no _call_lib_func_struct_in/_out, no _emit_byval_call, no _build_packed_interval); 191 docstrings use duckdb.org api.html anchors. README.md contains only project blurb + examples narrative and had no accuracy defects in scope. duckdb.h link on CLAUDE.md:30 is a bare file link at v1.3.2 (no line anchor) and is not itself broken; the defect there is the step1-vs-step5 contradiction (DOC-acc-5). The understanding note bindings.md independently corroborates the CLAUDE.md staleness (its 'Doc drift' section).
